slices.name: Grounded draft chat
slices.story: As a support analyst, I type a customer's product question into the chat and get back a draft answer that is grounded in our embedded product-knowledge documents, is clearly labelled as an automated draft pending my approval, and cites the doc ids it used — and when the question is not covered by the corpus the assistant says so and hands it back to me instead of guessing. This is the walking feature: chat-shell UI -> POST /chat -> agent_runtime.respond() -> reply rendered in the thread. It seeds agents/corpus_index.json with a small embedded product-knowledge corpus whose documents carry 'doc-' ids (including a password-reset doc), teaches the support_draft_agent persona from agents/roster.json in every mode (the deterministic stub included, since tests, acceptance and evals all run with HARNESS_AGENT_MODE=stub), and replaces the scaffold placeholder agents/evals/cases.json with the roster's support_draft_agent eval_cases. POST /chat must keep accepting a bare {"message": ...} and keep returning a "reply" key so the base test suite and the compose smoke keep passing.

slices.name: Conversation history behind analyst sign-in
slices.story: As a support analyst, every exchange I have with the assistant is saved as a structured conversation with its individual messages (role, content, timestamp), and I can open a History screen to list past conversations and read any one of them message by message — but only once signed in with my local analyst account; an unauthenticated caller gets 401 and never sees stored history. The client supplies a stable conversation_id on POST /chat (optional — a bare {"message": ...} still works and still returns "reply"), and rows are written through db.store into the conversations and messages tables from the approved data model. Reads of stored history live outside /api/ (GET /conversations, GET /conversations/{id}) so the /api/{table} catch-all does not shadow them, and accept the analyst session as a ?token= query parameter (a seeded local account, e.g. token 'analyst1' -> analyst-1) so the credential never has to ride in a header. Retention is indefinite: there is no purge, so history returns everything ever stored.

slices.name: Draft approval gate
slices.story: As a support analyst, the assistant's answer arrives as a draft that is never delivered on its own: I see it in the chat with an approve / edit / reject control, and nothing counts as sent until I act. Approving records approval_state, approved_by and approved_at on the drafts row (optionally with my edited text replacing the assistant's), rejecting records the rejection, and the approval response reminds me that delivery is a manual copy into the existing ticketing tool — the agent holds no send tool. Approval is analyst-only and authenticated: POST /approvals without a valid analyst session is rejected with 401, and draft reads (GET /drafts?conversation_id=...) require the same session as history. New endpoints live outside /api/ to avoid the /api/{table} catch-all.

slices.name: History keyword search and filter
slices.story: As a support analyst, instead of manually scrolling old threads I search history from the History screen: a keyword box and an approval-state filter narrow the conversation list, matching on message content and topic across the full retained history. A query that matches nothing returns 200 with a plain 'no matching prior conversation' message rather than an empty mystery, and search is gated by the same analyst session as the rest of history — an unauthenticated search is 401.

slices.name: Precedent lookup and reuse
slices.story: As a support analyst working a new question, I ask the precedent_finder from the History screen for a good prior answer, and it returns only approved replies with their provenance — source conversation id, approving analyst, approval date — plus a reminder to verify the answer is still accurate before reusing it, and says 'no matching prior conversation' when nothing matches rather than inventing one. One click carries that precedent into my current conversation as a new draft that records where it came from and is still pending my approval, so a reused answer never bypasses the approval gate. The precedent agent is the roster's second agent, reachable through agent_runtime with its own persona and eval cases wired into agents/evals/cases.json; every precedent path requires a signed-in analyst account and holds no send or approve tool.
